column1: # parser/spec/divergent.tsv — the parity debt, one row per divergence.
# One row per source, tab-separated:  src <TAB> go <TAB> ts <TAB> note
# Same comment and escaping rules as parse.tsv.
# Sources where parser/go and parser/ts render DIFFERENTLY. Each runner
# asserts its OWN column, so both suites stay green while the difference stays
# pinned: if either engine moves, its column fails and the row is re-examined
# rather than silently re-baselined. Each runner also FAILS a row whose go and
# ts columns are equal — a fixed divergence must MOVE to parse.tsv, or this
# file stops being an honest debt list.
# SHRINK-ONLY. Adding a row needs the justification a //covergate:allow does
# (design/COVERAGE-ALLOWLIST.10.md): a reviewed reason the difference is not
# simply a bug. Every row below is UNTRIAGED — recorded by
# design/TS-PARITY-AUDIT.0.md, not adjudicated against REFERENCE.md. The `go`
# column is the reference by convention, not by proof, and the rows marked
# DATA are behavioural rather than cosmetic: one engine is wrong.

column3: ERR [boru/evaluation_limit]: source nesting exceeds the depth limit of 500 — lists, maps, and parentheses are nested too deeply
column4: DATA: TS refuses at 501 where Go accepts to 10000 — the tabnas rule engine recurses per level and blows the JS call stack near 900, so the TS bound turns an uncontrolled RangeError into the promised evaluation_limit. Irreducible: raising it to Go(apos)s 10000 crashes (measured: 600 parses, 1000 overflows).

column1: # --- the TS rule-step cap: an error Go names and TS cannot ----------------
# The tabnas TS rule engine bounds its main loop and, on reaching the
# bound, simply STOPS: the trailing-token check then sees #ZZ, so nothing
# is thrown and the partial root is returned. The Go engine instead names
# the offending token. Every shape below leaves a group open with a
# terminator that cannot close it, so the TS val rule's implicit-null
# alternate matches the `]`, backtracks, and the enclosing elem re-pushes
# until the bound.
# Until the step-cap guard in parse(), TS ACCEPTED all of these: `[Map<]`
# parsed to an EMPTY value stream and `Map<]` to a bare `word(Map)`. The
# guard turns that silent wrong answer into the right CODE (syntax_error
# on both sides), so what is left here is error TEXT alone.
# Irreducible in this port: it is what the two ENGINES do, not what the
# two boru ports do. Closing it means the TS engine reporting the token
# it gave up on.
[Map<]
column2: ERR [boru/syntax_error]: unexpected `]` — nothing valid can appear here
column3: ERR [boru/syntax_error]: the parser could not make progress here — a group is left open by a `]`, `}` or end of input that cannot close it
column4: DATA: TS hits the rule-step cap and cannot name the token; same code, different text.
